summary:
The bench is built, calibrated on rules with a known verdict, and has judged the three new rules. Turning plane, along passes all eight basilica tests; Turning plane, away fails J8 (ribbed skin); the pure winding fails J4 and J8. Stage 2 was run only for "along", and its Mandelbrot solid fails: by eye it is a lumpy rock with ridges and a few horns, not a body carrying smaller round bodies. By the user's protocol the record is "Turning plane, along: basilica passes, Mandelbrot fails", and the search goes back to stage 1 with another rule.

findings: Turning plane, along is the only new rule whose basilica passes all eight tests. By eye it is the reference look with more buds: smooth round bodies, eight buds round the middle body, rows of small buds on each bud, both cuts z = 0 and y = 0 the flat basilica, no ribs (0.04 to 0.06 %).

Two things about 'along' that the pass lines hide. First, its small bodies are less round than the reference's and get less round with depth: 0.74, 0.56, 0.52, then 0.47 one size deeper (reference 0.74, 0.71, 0.74, 0.73). They are short pegs and lemon shapes in clusters, still bodies on bodies and not streaks by eye, but 0.52 to 0.56 lies in the band the calibration does not decide (known bad rules are at most 0.34, known good at least 0.71). Second, on J3 a 45 degree turn changes only 2.5 % of it (reference 6.0 %, lathe 0.0 %) because its eight buds are nearly equal; a 22.5 degree turn changes 8.5 % and nothing that comes off goes round the axis.

Turning plane, away, the one that looks most like the reference from afar (4 buds), fails J8: its bodies are ribbed like a melon and a bud cut across is a cog wheel. The ribs sit in a band about 20 degrees either side of each diagonal between the two planes and the skin is smooth near the planes (seen in the outline plot, not put into a number). Everything else passes.
The pure winding fails J4 and J8: ribbed lemon-shaped bodies, nothing round comes off.

The Mandelbrot solid of 'along' fails stage 2. Its cuts at z = 0 and y = 0 are both exactly the flat Mandelbrot set and it is one symmetric piece, but the solid itself is a lumpy rock with ridges and a few horns. What comes off it are ridges and fins (roundness 0.15 to 0.29), two of them running all the way round the axis, and the period-2 body is fused to the main body instead of touching at a point.

So this round's record, in the user's own format: 'Turning plane, along: basilica passes, Mandelbrot fails, because the solid is a lumpy rock with ridges; nothing round comes off it and the period-2 body is grown onto the main body.' The search goes back to stage 1 with another rule.

A good basilica does not predict a good Mandelbrot solid. 'Along' has the cleanest basilica of anything tested, yet its Julia sets for c off the x-axis are already lumps: the rabbit has volume 1.67 (the one-plane rabbit was 0.45 in the scout) and looks like one swollen ridged lump; the two c values off the flat plane give craggy lumps with 1.3 % and 2.7 % in loose pieces. This is measured for this one rule; that it holds in general is my reading, not a result.
None of the three new rules tears: largest jump about 1e-8 over a gap of 1e-9, and no jump at the x-axis. The close-pair numbers match the brief's (2.6e-3, 2.9e-4, 2.5e-5 for along).
The square pillow also fails J3 on this bench (a collar round the axis comes off, visible in its front view). That was not in the brief's list of known failures; it agrees with the picture.

A measure that cannot be taken (for example a rib outline when the bud has no clear body) counts as a fail in the J8 line. That is deliberate but could fail a future rule for the wrong reason; the sheet shows 'none' when it happens.

summary:
Both turning-plane rules are now entries in the lab ("Turning plane, away" and "Turning plane, along", group Sphere inversions, end of the list, no dials), checked by numbers and drawn. Started 18:57, finished 20:05 (about 68 minutes, of which about 15 were a stall of the machine).

Blunt picture verdict (stage 1 is the bench's to judge; this is what the lab's pictures and my point-by-point cuts show):
- AWAY, basilica: separate bodies with four buds, like the two-plane reference, touching at single points. But close up the skin is combed streaks and hair with small bumps, not smaller bodies, and thin whiskers stand off the bodies beside the planes y = z and y = -z. By my pictures it fails "close up, detail is smaller bodies, not streaks". On top of that the lab draws this rule as a streaked spindle of fog at the settings the page opens with; it only shows the bodies when "Distance estimate" is set to "Rough".
- ALONG, basilica: separate bodies with eight buds, touching at single points; the buds carry rings of smaller buds all round, at three depths, confirmed by point-by-point cuts. The bodies are ribbed and the buds have spiky crowns, so not smooth round bodies. The page's own scorecard says 39 % of directions land mirror-reversed (the rule folds space over).
- Beyond the basilica (not a stage-2 verdict): AWAY rabbit = curved shards in pieces, Mandelbrot solid = two thin crossed leaves with feathery shards. ALONG rabbit = one swollen layered lump, Mandelbrot solid = a lumpy layered rock with horns on eight corners and no round bulbs.
- Powers: the count round the x-axis follows the power for both (away 2n, along 4n), but for "away" only after I changed the brief's formula (the plane must turn n - 1 times as fast; with the brief's q = -1 it does not work at power 3, measured).

One check missed its target: the page's cut at z = 0 is NOT pixel for pixel the one-plane picture (see not_done).

findings: AWAY, basilica, what I saw: with the Rough estimate a row of separate bodies, each with a bud above, below, in front and behind, same layout as Sphere inversions, two planes. At 60 steps the neck between two bodies is gone and they meet in one point; the cut across that point at 40 steps is empty but for the point. Not rings, not a spun flat set. A bud has smaller buds to its sides (cut x = 0 through the bud). BUT close up at three depths the skin is combed streaks and hair with small round bumps between, not smaller bodies; the level cut through the bud has a fuzzy rim with rays; cuts show thin whiskers off the bodies beside the planes y = z and y = -z, thinning to specks at 40 steps. In the diagonal plane y = z the bodies have no buds at all.

ALONG, basilica, what I saw: separate bodies with eight buds round the x-axis, two in each of four planes; bodies meet in one point (60 steps, and the 40-step cut). Close up at three depths: ribbed bodies, and each bud carries rings of smaller buds all round, not only in the flat plane; cuts show the same smaller buds and a round bud with small spikes all round. The buds are spiky and ribbed, not smooth balls. Exact and Rough draw the same shapes, except for the false flat sheet Exact adds beside the touching points.

The page's own scorecard at power 2 (card.txt): away: roundness 54 %, stretch at |v| = 1 from 0 to 9.9 times where the plane gives 2, covers the sphere of directions 4 times, 4 % mirror-reversed, net wrap 4. along: roundness 60 %, stretch 0 to 6 times, covers the sphere 3.2 times, 39 % of directions mirror-reversed, net wrap 0. So "along" folds space over a great deal; in the planes y = +-z the sideways stretch passes through zero on the lines 60 degrees from the x-axis (measured).

Sphere inversions, two planes, drawn the same way for comparison: smooth creased bodies, four buds, buds in rows along four lines; its neck behaves the same (single point at 60 steps, empty cut at 40 steps). At 14 to 26 steps ALL three rules show a neck between the bodies; that is the step count, not the rule.

Beyond the basilica, as seen (stage 2 not judged here). AWAY: rabbit breaks into curved shards and separate pieces (the cut across shows islands); c = (-1, 0.15, 0.1) a ragged streaked lump; Mandelbrot solid = two thin leaves crossed along the x-axis (in z = 0 and y = 0) with feathery shards, cut at x = -0.2 is a small lump with a thin cross (9 % of a 2.4 window at 14 steps, 6 % at 40), no bulbs off the two planes. ALONG: rabbit one swollen layered lump, no separate bodies; c off the plane a chain of ragged lumps; Mandelbrot solid one lumpy layered rock with horns on eight corners and the flat set's spike, no round bulbs; its cut at x = -0.2 is a filled rounded diamond (39 % of the window at 14 steps, 29 % at 40) whose edges turn dusty at 40 steps; cuts at z = 0, y = 0 and y = z are the flat Mandelbrot set.

Powers: for c on the x-axis the count round the axis follows the power. away: power 3, c = 0.3 a six-sided lump; power 4, c = -1 a body with eight buds (cut: eight buds); power 3 Mandelbrot solid three thin leaves crossed (six blades seen along the x-axis). along: power 3 Mandelbrot solid has twelve horns; power 4, c = -1 a lens-shaped body with sixteen small buds on one rim (cut: sixteen). Power 3 with c = (0, 1, 0): away is shards, along a lumpy cross-shaped rock. So the smear at higher powers is not cured: the count is right, the surfaces are not bodies on bodies.

The lab's "Exact" distance estimate is not reliable for either rule: fog for away, false sheets on the diagonal planes for along. "Rough" agrees with the point-by-point cuts in every place I compared (basilica x = 0, the bud, the touching point). Rough may still skip things thinner than its steps: the whiskers of away show in the cuts more clearly than in any 3D picture.
The scout's rough voxel pictures (257 a side) made "away" look clean because the whiskers are thinner than a voxel. Anything judging J5 or J8 for it needs finer cuts.

J9, as built: the only count in the rule is m, the whole number nearest to the power (at least 1), so it follows the power. That m = n and not m = 2 at every power is the orchestrator's choice; the texts say it is a choice made so the count follows the power.

The 2D view of the page is not a pure test of the plane z = 0: it shades edges from samples slightly off the plane, so a rule that is exact on the plane can still differ from the one-plane picture at a few hundred edge pixels (my reading of the code, not proven).

risks: The first picture a user sees for "Turning plane, away" is wrong (fog) unless they change a quality setting. This is the biggest risk of shipping the entry as it is.

The Rough estimate is the page's least accurate one by its own label. It agreed with point-by-point cuts wherever I compared, but it can step over things thinner than its steps, so Rough pictures may flatter "away" by hiding whiskers. The cuts are the safer evidence.
All close-ups are of one bud (the one on top of the middle body) and one touching point, at three depths, for c = -1 only. Other places were not looked at close up.
The pixel counts quoted in the entry notes (748, 35, 68 of 604,262) belong to one picture size (862 x 701), 14 steps and the opening 2D frame; at other sizes the numbers will differ.

GPU trigonometry limits the shader to about 8e-5 of the length at power 2 (1.7e-4 at powers 3 and 4) against the 64-bit rule. Deep zooms with many steps may show this as fine noise; not tested beyond camera distance 0.06 and 26 steps (60 steps at distance 0.25).

Powers above 5, and powers that are not whole, were not drawn; planes were measured for powers 2 to 5 only. A power that is not whole takes the planes of the nearest whole number, so the picture jumps between whole powers (said in the text).
